prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1493; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound in the left lane of a two-lane road in Conroe, Texas, when the vehicle crossed the center line and struck the northbound vehicle operated by Driver 2 in a low-speed head-on collision. Driver 1 was the sole occupant of the vehicle at the time of impact, and this was confirmed by the responding officer, by two independent witnesses who stopped at the scene, and by Driver 2. Driver 1 reported neck strain and was evaluated by emergency medical personnel on scene, who noted that the complaint is consistent with the forward and rearward motion typical of a collision of this type. Both witnesses independently described the impact as occurring exactly as Driver 1 and Driver 2 later related it. Scene photographs show front-end damage to both vehicles that matches the direction and force of the reported impact. No prior damage to the vehicle was noted by the officer or disclosed by either party. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. No citations were issued at the scene, and the vehicles were towed from the roadway.
